ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC, AB=5, BC=7, then what is the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AC$, \\
$\therefore$ $AD=DC$, \\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$ is $AD+BD+AB=DC+BD+AB=BC+AB=5+7=\boxed{12}$

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: A, B, C form a triangle, D lies on side BC, and segment AD is one side of triangle ABD; the line through D and E meets AC at E. From the text, use that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC, with AB=5 and BC=7. Since any point on the perpendicular bisector of AC is equidistant from A and C, point D satisfies AD=DC. Then the perimeter of triangle ABD is AB+BD+AD = AB+BD+DC. Because D is on BC in the image, BD+DC=BC, so the perimeter is AB+BC=5+7=12.
